boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study environments in FAU’s S.E. Wimberly Library, selected for quiet work, collaboration, technology, accessibility, or extended access.

cards.entity_name: Wimberly Library First-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.title: First-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Quiet work near the main level of S.E. Wimberly Library
cards.notes: Choose this designated quiet area when you need a straightforward solo setup; confirm the day’s library hours before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet zone on Wimberly Library’s first floor for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries identifies the first floor of S.E. Wimberly Library as a recommended quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Test and Exam Proctoring Policy | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located inside S.E. Wimberly Library; building entry and availability are governed by current library access rules and hours.

cards.entity_name: Wimberly Library Third-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.title: Third-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: A designated quiet floor with nearby reservable rooms
cards.notes: Set up here for quiet independent work, or reserve a nearby third-floor room separately when your session requires conversation.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study destination that keeps reservable collaboration rooms within the same floor.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries designates Wimberly Library’s third floor as a quiet study area and separately lists reservable rooms on that floor.
cards.source_title: Test and Exam Proctoring Policy | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the open quiet area during library hours; enclosed third-floor study rooms follow separate reservation and Owl Card rules.

cards.entity_name: Wimberly Library Fourth Floor East Silent Study Area
cards.title: Fourth Floor East Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Wimberly Library’s explicitly designated silent zone
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from minimal conversation and use the carrels or seating while observing the area’s silent-study designation.
cards.short_summary: An explicitly designated silent area suited to reading, writing, and exam preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries recommends Fourth Floor East in S.E. Wimberly Library as a silent study area.
cards.source_title: Test and Exam Proctoring Policy | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available while the library is open; users should follow the space’s silent-study expectation.

cards.entity_name: Wimberly Library Fifth Floor East Video Conference Study Rooms
cards.title: Fifth Floor East Video Conference Rooms
cards.subtitle: Private rooms for recorded or remotely proctored work
cards.notes: Reserve ahead when privacy matters; otherwise ask at the Service Desk about first-come availability and the one-hour use period.
cards.short_summary: Reservable enclosed rooms designed for video-enabled study and assessment needs.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries lists Fifth Floor East video conference study rooms as reservable in advance or available through the Service Desk for one hour on a first-come basis.
cards.source_title: Test and Exam Proctoring Policy | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve in advance or request a room from the Service Desk; stated use is one hour and first-come when not reserved.

cards.title: Graduate Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Owl Card-controlled space on the second-floor west end
cards.notes: Use this lounge if you meet the eligibility rules; choose computer stations, partitioned cubicles, collaboration tables, or sofa seating.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated graduate and medical-student lounge with varied seating and computer options.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU documents a second-floor Graduate Study Lounge with computer stations, collaboration space, private cubicles, sofas, tables, outlets, and Owl Card-controlled access.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to eligible graduate and Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine students; entry is controlled by Owl Card.

cards.title: ADA Group Study Room LY 251
cards.subtitle: Accessible study room with adaptive equipment
cards.notes: Coordinate access through Student Accessibility Services, then bring a valid card and plan around the room’s two-hour checkout window.
cards.short_summary: A reservable accessible room equipped for students registered with accessibility services.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries states that LY 251 offers Fusion, Read&Write, a high-contrast keyboard, adaptable lighting, and an adjustable desk for registered SAS students.
cards.source_title: Circulation: Policies and Services | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Students must be registered with Student Accessibility Services and coordinate access through their SAS coordinator; checkout is two hours with a valid card.

cards.title: Rubin and Cindy Gruber Sandbox
cards.subtitle: First-floor technology workspace for AI projects
cards.notes: Bring an AI-related course or research project during posted open hours and use the high-performance computers or visualization equipment.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich collaborative workspace open to students across academic disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU describes the first-floor Sandbox as a collaborative AI space with high-performance computers, VR headsets, and high-resolution monitors.
cards.source_title: Interested in AI? Check out Sandbox Open Hours | FAU Libraries
cards.access_notes: The official page lists open hours Monday through Friday, 1–5 p.m., for students, faculty, staff, and community members; verify before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Wimbish Wing First-Floor 24-Hour Student Study Center
cards.title: First-Floor 24-Hour Study Center
cards.subtitle: Extended-access workspace in Wimberly Library’s Wimbish Wing
cards.notes: Use this first-floor center when regular library spaces are unavailable, and keep your Owl Card ready for controlled building access.
cards.short_summary: One of two student study centers identified by FAU as providing around-the-clock access.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries identifies a 24-hour student study center on the first floor of Wimberly Library’s Wimbish Wing.
cards.access_notes: FAU identifies this as a 24-hour student study center; carry a valid Owl Card and check current access notices before an overnight visit.

cards.entity_name: Wimbish Wing Second-Floor 24-Hour Student Study Center
cards.title: Second-Floor 24-Hour Study Center
cards.subtitle: A separate extended-access floor in the Wimbish Wing
cards.notes: Head to the second-floor center for another extended-access option, carrying your Owl Card and checking campus closure notices first.
cards.short_summary: A distinct second-floor study center maintained for continuous student access.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries identifies a 24-hour student study center on the second floor of Wimberly Library’s Wimbish Wing.
cards.access_notes: FAU identifies this as a 24-hour student study center; Owl Card access and temporary campus or building closures may still apply.

cards.title: Study Room 326
cards.subtitle: Online-reservable collaboration room on the third floor
cards.notes: Reserve online before arriving, include the required participants, and allow time for the booking to activate before swiping in.
cards.short_summary: A specifically numbered third-floor room supporting reserved individual or collaborative sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU Libraries lists Room 326 among the third-floor rooms available through its online study-room reservation system.
cards.access_notes: Online reservations are limited to FAU students, faculty, and staff. Group entry requires two reserved users to swipe Owl Cards; individual requests are limited to one or two hours daily.
